title: Per-pixel features 26 -> 50: in-domain LOCO
why: Does expanding the per-pixel feature vector from 26 to 50 improve IndEgo LOCO accuracy?
hypothesis: Added features raise in-domain AUROC above 0.810
data: IndEgo gold 150 windows (7 clips), manifest_gold.json + caches/gpu/features.json

title: Per-pixel features 26 -> 50: OOD adapted
why: Does the 50-feature set improve OOD-160 adapted z-score over 0.781?
hypothesis: Additional transferable features raise OOD AUROC
data: OOD-160 human labels (138/22, 47 factories); adapted per-domain z-score
method: per-domain z-score, IndEgo sign, equal-weight mean; factory-grouped bootstrap

title: Ablation of the 24 added features
why: Which added feature families carry the gain; is there saturation?
hypothesis: A few families dominate; saturation after ~6-10 features

title: Hold-out108 scored once (26 vs 50)
why: Honest generalisation check of the 50-feature recipe
hypothesis: Gain replicates weakly or not at all
method: frozen per-domain z-score recipe, no tuning

title: Cost of the 24 added features
why: Edge budget: ms/window of the added kernels

summary: In-domain LOCO 0.810 (26) -> 0.787 (50), delta -0.023 (ns). No in-domain gain.
OOD-160 adapted: documented 14-feat 0.781; +18 new 0.657 (-0.123 [-0.224,-0.035], sig. worse); all-50 0.512. No transferable gain.
Ablation: only dct_bands (0.728 alone) and edge_lap (0.680) carry OOD signal; saturation immediate (0.781->0.779->...->0.657).
Hold-out108 scored once: documented 0.676; +18 new 0.612; all-50 0.457. Gain does not replicate.
Added cost 148 ms/window (18 kernels 43 ms + ffprobe 104 ms); decode 157 ms shared.
